reports.title: dLocal Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Guidance 2026: where we stand
section: 1.TPV growth remains strong, moderating as expected against tougher comps;

2.Operating profit negatively affected by unanticipated FX headwinds at the revenue and gross profit level in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina and softer performance in smaller high take rate markets in Africa & Asia;

desk.headline: Revenue up 41% to $398m, below estimates; EPS $0.23 beat; 2026 operating profit now seen at low end of range
results: Payment volume grew 77% to $18.3bn, the eighth straight quarter above 50% growth; revenue rose 41% to $398m but was flat on the second quarter as Argentina volumes eased after a seasonal peak.
Gross profit hit a record $132m (+28%), but the margin fell to 33% from 37% as more volume came from lower-fee local and payout flows and costs rose in Brazil and Mexico.
Operating costs fell 11% from the second quarter to $55.9m, lifting operating profit 37% to $76m and net income 31% to a record $68m.
Adjusted free cash flow was $99m in the quarter and $182m in nine months.
dLocal bought back about $34m of shares in the quarter (about $120m so far this year) and drew a $150m loan in August.

guidance.summary: dLocal kept the 2026 ranges it set with its Q2 results and said where it expects to land: TPV growth toward the top of 60–70%, gross profit growth around the middle of 25–30%, and operating profit growth toward the low end of 27.5–32.5%, hurt by unexpected currency moves in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.

points: Management expects currency headwinds in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina in the fourth quarter, worth about 6 points of year-on-year gross profit growth.
It said the squeeze on fees per transaction is starting to slow.
Part of the cost cut is lasting (lower payroll and outside spending) and part is timing, such as marketing spent earlier in the year.
In Mexico, higher processing costs and catch-up charges hurt gross profit; management said fixing this should not take several quarters.
Management said the heavy investment phase is over and it expects gross profit to grow faster than costs on a yearly basis.

watch: Fourth-quarter gross profit as currency headwinds hit Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.
Whether gross profit per dollar of volume (0.72%) stabilises as mix shifts to lower-fee flows.
Whether operating costs stay near the lower third-quarter level.
